summary: Implement the frozen React/TypeScript/Vite frontend shell and finalize the developer-surface runtime decision for server state, host-owned OIDC authentication, capability-aware routing and generated SDK consumption.

impacts.evidence: The shell never accepts or synthesizes organization/workspace selectors; API tenant/workspace scope remains derived from authenticated server context.
Browser state contains bounded public projections only. Access-token material stays in memory and is excluded from the public UI-session schema and persistence APIs.
The frontend consumes only the generated Task-062 TypeScript SDK and current public OpenAPI operations; no hand-written endpoint contract or copied generated client is introduced.
Task 032 does not publish or mutate event envelopes or event payload contracts.
Connector SDK and provider runtime contracts are unchanged; the shell does not import connector implementations.
No database schema or migration is introduced; browser state is non-authoritative.

Host-owned OIDC adapter, memory-only access tokens, exact capability route guards, same-origin SDK transport, redirect rejection, and static checks prevent browser persistence, tenant-selector injection and provider-specific branching.
Navigation metadata preserves risk class for sensitive areas, but approval authorization remains server-side Task-017 policy and no sensitive write is implemented by the shell.
Audit and lineage remain server-owned API/domain capabilities; the shell does not duplicate evidence stores.
Task 032 adds no sync/reconciliation mutation semantics and does not alter request idempotency contracts.
The browser does not send durable webhooks or duplicate Task-063 egress; Notifications reads use the public API only.
Frontend loading/error states are deterministic, but production browser telemetry/SLO instrumentation remains later operational work and no SLO claim is made.
The shell is a static artifact behind same-origin hosting; rollback is deployment of the prior bundle/API-compatible commit. No data rollback is required.

frontend-check adds capability/session/decoder tests, TSX repository validation and static security checks; a real Vite bundle is additionally required when npm dependencies are installed in CI/staging.
